representation: A positive and a negative point charge with local field arrows around each, plus a movable test dot on their perpendicular bisector whose single arrow shows the net field.
motion: The test dot slides vertically along the centre line; the net-field arrow stays horizontal by symmetry and changes length with inverse-square distance.
checkpoints: field points away from positive and toward negative charge
net field arrow shortens with distance
the two contributions add as vectors
field is not force on a particular test charge
sample vectors are not crossing field lines
misconceptionTest: The moving net-field arrow is labelled E and described as force per unit positive test charge, with a note that a negative test charge would feel the opposite force. Separate sample arrows are used instead of continuous field lines, and a checkpoint explains why distinct field lines cannot cross.
accessibility: Alt text; keyboard slider; arrows have text labels; charge signs are written as plus and minus, not color-only.
